valuation.method: Mid-cycle EPS x P/E per ADS. Petrobras reports in BRL; 1 PBR ADS = 1 common share (ratio 1:1 for the common ADS; preferred ADS is a separate line, not used). FX assumed 5.17 BRL/USD, derived from Q3 2026 net income R$39.8bn = about US$7.7bn (reported coverage, Nov 2026), no independent dated rate pulled. Roughly 12.9bn shares. FY2027 EPS viewed at the Nov 2027 target date. Price-only; dividends excluded (R$1.1873/share for Q3 = about $0.23).

bear.driver: Brent falls toward $60, export tax and Brazil policy/political risk persist, payouts shrink

base.driver: Q3 2026 run-rate (net income R$39.8bn, production 3.51m boe/d) partly normalised for lower oil; payout 45% of FCF

bull.driver: Oil near current levels (Brent about $95), production 3.3-3.4m boe/d guidance met, clean strategic plan on Nov 23

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $2.20 the close of $18.34 implies 8.3x; the Morgan Stanley $25 target implies 11.4x or EPS $2.94 at 8.5x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $2.20 (12.0 pp of the close).
valuation.watch_metric: Brent realised price and quarterly net income against R$39.8bn, plus the payout under the 45% FCF policy
valuation.next_disclosure: Strategic plan due 2026-11-23; Q4 2026 results in early 2027

analyst_notes: Only Morgan Stanley's post-Q3 cut (target $31 to $25, still top-rated) is dated after the 2026-11 results; others are older 2026 calls. Analyst names are not published in sources, targets have undocumented horizons so they are excluded from the weighted target. Gap to base case: $25 requires about $2.94 EPS at 8.5x, or 11.4x on base EPS.
